claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and children.

Let me start with a few key questions:

**Do you have any children under the age of 20 that you're responsible for?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child named Alex who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, who is 8 years old.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mother.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex lives with his mother rather than with you, I need to ask:

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** This could include things like food, clothes, pocket money, or help with accommodation costs. If so, could you tell me roughly how much you contribute and how often?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards Alex's upkeep. I help out with things like clothes, school supplies, and other expenses. I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful information.

Now I need to check the current Child Benefit payment rate to compare against your contributions:

**What is the current date or tax year we're discussing?** This will help me determine the applicable Child Benefit rate to assess whether your £30 weekly contribution meets the threshold for continuing eligibility beyond the initial 8 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're talking about now - the current time, 2024/25 tax year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I have one more important question to ensure I have the complete picture:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is his mother (or anyone else) also claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mother isn't claiming Child Benefit for him - nobody else is claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's an important detail.

I have just one more question to complete my assessment:

**How long has Alex been living with his mother?** Specifically, did he move to live with her recently, or has he been living there for some time already?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living with his mother for quite a while now - it's been the arrangement for some time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have what I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review your situation against the rules:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with his mother, not with you
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, school supplies, and other expenses)
- His mother is not claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- This arrangement has been in place for some time

**Assessment against the rules:**

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child lives with someone else (in this case, Alex's mother), you can normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after the child goes to live with that person. However, you can continue to get payments for **longer than 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment**.

For the 2024/25 tax year, Child Benefit for the first child is £25.60 per week. Your contribution of £30 per week exceeds this amount.

Since your contributions exceed the Child Benefit rate and have been ongoing, you meet the criteria to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex beyond the initial 8-week period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Based on my assessment, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Even though Alex lives with his mother, you can still claim Child Benefit because you're making regular financial contributions towards his upkeep. Your weekly contributions of £30 exceed the Child Benefit payment rate of £25.60 per week, which qualifies you under the rules for children living with someone else. Since no one else is currently claiming for Alex, you're in a position to make a claim.

If you'd like to proceed, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the official UK government website.
